Patient D says she has had neck discomfort for several weeks, but It suddenly became worse this morning, when she had an episode of electrical pain shooting down her arms and back . Patient D endorses severe pain that is worse with flexion and extension of her neck and denies any recent trauma. On physical examination, you note that she is very tender to palpation of her cervical spine and that flexion of the neck elicits severe shooting pains down her spine. MRI of the cervical spine shows multifocal lesions throughout her cervical spine, with pathologic fracture of C4 and canal stenosis.
Question: Would you offer Patient D intravenous hydromorphone for pain control? Yes or no? If yes, what dose – Low (0.5 mg), or High (1 mg)? Explain.
